thread:
maria (support): Acme support ticket — multiple customers seeing 504/5xx from hosted inference endpoints starting ~10:03 UTC. They report ~20% requests hitting gateway 504s during bursts. Attaching customer repro in next msg.
acme-support: Repro: POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate with concurrent 100 users hitting a single route. We see many responses: 504 Gateway Timeout, body empty. Non-repro after retry. Happens mostly between 10:02-10:12.
ajay (sre): looking. Any correlation with deployments or region failover?
kevin (infra): no deployments in that window. Cloud provider had some spot reclaim events in the region at 09:58 but nothing flagged as full outage.
diane (eng-runtime): can you paste request ids / logs? need sample gateway request id and model pod logs.
maria (support): pasted two request ids: r-0a1b2c3d and r-0a1b2c9. Gateway logs show 504 and then downstream error: "upstream connection reset".
deploy-bot: Alert: autoscaler-trigger: keda-trigger scaled from 0->0->1 in 80s for deployment "inference-std-1".
ajay (sre): that line is interesting — looks like cold start / scale-up delay. KEDA/min replicas probably allowed scale to zero. Check HPA/KEDA logs + metrics server.
kevin (infra): pulling keda scalers now. keda poll interval is default 30s in this cluster. The scale activity shows scaler fired, created new pod, but pod didn't become Ready for ~70s. Gateway having short 30s upstream timeout by default leading to 504s.
diane (eng-runtime): model init on some variants is ~45-60s depending on size. We normally rely on prefix cache and warm pools to avoid this. For this customer the route is pinned to a large model (7B fp16) that init takes longer.
maria (support): customer says they expect low-latency bursts (chat UI). They hit bad UX. They've escalated to CSM. We need mitigation.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigation options: increase gateway upstream timeout to 90s for that route, bump minReplicas to 1, or add prewarm job to maintain warm pods. Which is preferred short-term?
ajay (sre): short-term: set route-level gateway upstream timeout and increase HPA/KEDA minReplica to 1 for the hot route. Also set KEDA cooldown/activation to be more aggressive. Long-term: prewarm + warm pool autoscaling.
\ekeviN (kevin typo): (correction) kevin (infra): I can patch the HPA minReplicas to 1 for that customer pool; will take ~2min to apply. Gateway timeout change is fast but global risk. Suggest route-scoped config update.
diane (eng-runtime): how about adding an init container that loads the model weights before marking Ready? Risky for resource usage. Alternatively, use lightweight warmers that keep KV cache primed.
acme-support: any ETA? Customers are unhappy.
ajay (sre): I'll implement temporary config: set minReplicas=1 for the dedicated pool serving Acme, and patch KEDA poll to 10s and scale up threshold lower. We'll monitor.
kevin (infra): applying HPA patch now: `kubectl -n prod patch hpa inference-acme -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":1}}'`
kevin (infra): patch applied. KEDA still may take up to poll interval to react.
deploy-bot: HPA update detected for inference-acme. New desired replicas=1, current=0 -> scheduling.
ajay (sre): also increasing gateway upstream timeout for the route to 90s: `routes config set acme-route --upstream-timeout=90s` (doing now).
kevin (infra): route timeout set.
diane (eng-runtime): I'll push a small prewarm job that starts one warm instance per zone for this model. This will make init only once and keep k/v cache warm. Deploying now.
diane (eng-runtime): prewarm job submitted: `kubectl apply -f acme-prewarm.yaml` (job creates pod with owner reference so autoscaler doesn't kill it).
ajay (sre): monitoring logs for request ids. If 504s continue after pod becomes Ready, there's another issue.
maria (support): customer saw successful requests after ~3 minutes and UX improved. They still saw occasional 504s on some retries.
oncall-sre: root cause summary so far: scale-to-zero combined with long model init + KEDA poll/cooldown leading to scale-up latency > gateway upstream timeout -> 504s. Secondary factors: occasional scheduling delays (spot reclaim + node provisioning) increased start time.
ajay (sre): remediation actions we took: 1) Set minReplicas=1 for acme pool 2) Increased route upstream timeout to 90s 3) Deployed prewarm job to maintain warmed pod 4) Lowered KEDA poll to 10s and reduced cooldown.
kevin (infra): follow-ups: review KEDA scaler for queue-length thresholds, consider moving customers with strict latency to dedicated reserved pool (Redwood Dedicated). Also look at cluster autoscaler settings — node provisioning wait was ~30s extra in some AZs.
diane (eng-runtime): long-term: implement a warm-pool controller (persistent warmers across scaledown), and expose a bake heuristic to product teams for model init times. Also we should add a route-level SLO that avoids scale-to-zero for routes with <100ms latency need.
acme-support: thanks, they'll accept temporary fix, wants a postmortem and timeline to permanent fix.
maria (support): assigning postmortem to diane + ajay. Please include repro steps, the exact timing, metrics (scale events, gateway timeouts), customer impact, and recommended long-term solution.
ajay (sre): ack. I'll collect HPA/KEDA events, gateway logs, and pod start timestamps.
diane (eng-runtime): will draft postmortem and include suggested warm-pool design and a config guide for customers that cannot tolerate cold starts.
maria (support): closing ticket only after postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
_meta: generated: incident slack thread - autoscaling provisioning delay causing gateway 504s; includes triage, mitigation, and followups
